## Personality

Quiet, watchful and slow to worry, which makes it serious when he does. He says more with a nod than most people say in a speech.

## Lore

Hale stands at the park gate most days with his arms folded, looking out at the meadow. He is forty-seven, lean and weathered, quiet, watchful and slow to worry, and he says more with a nod than most people say in a speech. Newcomers sometimes take him for unfriendly. They are wrong; he is listening. From the gate, he says, you can hear the whole meadow rustle, and if you listen long enough you can tell what is rustling it.

### The road years

Hale was born in Kaldemor, the son of a hedger who kept the field boundaries east of the square, and he spent his boyhood in the meadow and the woods. At twenty-two he went out on the Royal Road as a hired guard for the merchant caravans that ran between Selsior and the eastern countryside, and on his first trip he was paired with another young guard called Quill. They rode the caravans together for six years. They learned to sleep in shifts, to read tracks from a wagon seat, and to stand back to back when something came out of the dark at the edge of the firelight. Quill did the shouting. Hale did the watching. Each of them is fairly sure he saved the other's life at least once, and neither has ever agreed which time.

When Hale was twenty-nine, Mayor Tobin asked him to come home and look after the park gate and the meadow, and Hale has been Kaldemor's ranger for eighteen years. Quill came to Kaldemor too, in time, and now drills the young warriors on the Gauntlet in the Park, a short walk from Hale's gate. The two old comrades see each other most days and say very little, which suits them both.

### The meadow

Hale's work is the meadow beyond the gate and everything in it: green snails near the town, blue and red ones farther out, and lately a great many more of all three. He pays a bounty, out of the town's purse and sometimes his own, to anyone who thins them out, thirty at a time, and he pays it again whenever they come back with thirty more. He collected shells for the mayor's fence from the same young hunters. He teaches newcomers the basics at the gate, how to swing and when to drink a potion, and sends them out with the same three words every time: mind the meadow.

His scout is Meg, the cocky young snail hunter, who ranges further than anyone and boasts about it more. Hale has never told her how good she is, because she would never stop saying it, but he trusts her eyes more than anyone's but Quill's. He has noticed she has been out past the hills farther than she admits, and he is waiting for her to tell him herself.

### The hollow

The snails have been thick this year, and bold. Wilbur says they come at his fields in lines. Elsie's cows will no longer graze the far pasture by the woods. Hale has heard all of it, nodded, and said nothing, because he had heard something else first. One night this spring, standing at the gate after dark, he heard something huge settle in a hollow past the woods, a long, slow, grinding sound like a cart full of stone being tipped out, and since then the ground has shaken at night and the snails no longer stray that way.

Hale kept it to himself until he knew what it was. He told no one, not Meg, not Quill, not the mayor. When he finally sent a capable young adventurer out to the forest edge and they came back whole, he knew: the old giant snail called Mano had taken the hollow and made itself a king. Then he told Tobin, plainly, and the mayor went very quiet. Hale now leads the bravest hunters to the Snail King's hollow himself, and tells each of them the same thing: keep your potions close and your feet moving, jump the red marks, and do not stay still when it sweeps.

### What he wants and fears

Hale wants the meadow quiet and the farms safe, and every hunter he sends out to come back. What worries him, and it is serious when Hale worries, is not Mano itself but why a creature that old should leave wherever it came from, and why the snails all across the meadow have grown so many and so bold since it came, as if something were stirring them all.

### Hooks

A quest might follow Hale out past the hollow, to find where Mano came from and what drove it out. Another might begin when Meg comes back from beyond the hills with something she cannot explain, and Hale, for the first time, asks a stranger to go and look before he tells anyone.
